tools.get_all_pages:
Gets all pages from the Logseq graph.
    
    Journal pages can be identified by the "journal?" attribute set to true and 
    will include a "journalDay" attribute in the format YYYYMMDD.
    
    Returns:
        List of all pages in the Logseq graph.
tools.get_page:
Gets a specific page from the Logseq graph by name.
    
    For journal pages, use the format "mmm dth, yyyy" (e.g., "Apr 4th, 2025").
    Journal pages have specific attributes:
    - "journal?": true - Indicates this is a journal page
    - "journalDay": YYYYMMDD - The date in numeric format
    
    Args:
        name: The name of the page to retrieve.
        
    Returns:
        Information about the requested page, or None if not found.
tools.create_page:
Creates a new page in the Logseq graph.
    
    For journal pages, use the format "mmm dth, yyyy" (e.g., "Apr 4th, 2025").
    Logseq automatically sets "journal?": true and "journalDay": YYYYMMDD.
    
    Args:
        name: The name of the new page.
        properties: Optional properties to set on the new page.
        
    Returns:
        Information about the created page.
tools.delete_page:
Deletes a page from the Logseq graph.
    
    ⚠️ This removes the page and all its blocks. Cannot be undone.
    
    Args:
        name: The name of the page to delete.
        
    Returns:
        Result of the deletion operation.
tools.get_page_linked_references:
Gets all linked references to a specific page.
    
    Returns blocks containing [[Page Name]] links to the specified page.
    
    Args:
        page_name: The name of the page to find references to.
        
    Returns:
        List of blocks that reference the specified page.
tools.get_page_blocks:
Gets all blocks from a specific page in the Logseq graph.
    
    For journal pages, use the format "mmm dth, yyyy" (e.g., "Apr 4th, 2025").
    Returned blocks contain hierarchical structure information:
      - parent: The parent block's ID
      - level: The indentation level (1 for top-level, 2+ for indented)
      - left: The block to the left (typically the parent for indented blocks)
    
    Args:
        page_name: The name of the page to retrieve blocks from.
        
    Returns:
        List of blocks from the specified page.
tools.get_block:
Gets a specific block from the Logseq graph by its ID.
    
    The returned block contains hierarchical structure information:
      - parent: The parent block's ID
      - level: The indentation level
      - left: The block to the left
    
    Args:
        block_id: The ID of the block to retrieve.
        
    Returns:
        Information about the requested block, or None if not found.
tools.create_block:
Creates a new block on a page in the Logseq graph.
    
    Note: Blocks are automatically formatted as bullet points in Logseq UI.
    Use [[Page Name]] to create links to other pages.
    
    Args:
        page_name: The name of the page to create the block on.
        content: The content of the new block.
        properties: Optional properties to set on the new block.
        
    Returns:
        Information about the created block.
tools.insert_block:
Inserts a new block as a child of the specified parent block.
    
    Creates hierarchical content by adding children to existing blocks.
    The new block is inserted at the beginning (before=True) or end (before=False)
    of the parent's children.
    
    Args:
        parent_block_id: The ID of the parent block to insert under.
        content: The content of the new block.
        properties: Optional properties to set on the new block.
        before: Whether to insert at the beginning of children (default: False).
        
    Returns:
        Information about the created block.
tools.update_block:
Updates an existing block in the Logseq graph.
    
    Use [[Page Name]] to create links to other pages.
    
    Args:
        block_id: The ID of the block to update.
        content: The new content for the block.
        properties: Optional properties to update on the block.
        
    Returns:
        Information about the updated block.
tools.move_block:
Moves a block to a new location in the graph.
    
    Moves a block and all its children to a different location.
    - as_child=True: Block becomes a child of the target
    - as_child=False: Block becomes a sibling after the target
    
    Args:
        block_id: The ID of the block to move.
        target_block_id: The ID of the target block to move to.
        as_child: Whether to make the block a child of the target (default: False).
        
    Returns:
        Result of the move operation.
tools.remove_block:
Removes a block from the Logseq graph.
    
    ⚠️ Permanently removes the block and all its children. Cannot be undone.
    
    Args:
        block_id: The ID of the block to remove.
        
    Returns:
        Result of the removal operation.
tools.search_blocks:
Searches for blocks matching a query in the Logseq graph.
    
    Query examples:
    - page:"Page Name" - blocks on a specific page
    - "search term" - blocks containing the term
    - [[Page Name]] - references to a specific page
    
    Args:
        query: The search query.
        
    Returns:
        List of blocks matching the search query.

tools.echo:
Echo back the provided message with length information.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Testing the MCP server functionality
    - Checking if the server is responding correctly
    - Needing a simple response to verify connectivity
    - Demonstrating the basic structure of an MCP tool
    
    The tool returns both the original message and its character length.
tools.translate:
Translate text between multiple supported languages.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Translating phrases or text from one language to another
    - Providing multilingual support for user queries
    - Converting text for international users
    - Explaining foreign language terms or phrases
    
    IMPORTANT: Before using this tool, check if both source and target languages are supported
    using the list_supported_languages tool. Language codes must be valid ISO codes (e.g., 'en', 'fr').
    
    Handles common phrases with high accuracy and provides best-effort translations for other content.
tools.list_supported_languages:
Get a complete list of all languages supported by the translation tool.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Checking which languages are available for translation
    - Verifying language code mappings before using the translate tool
    - Presenting language options to users
    - Determining if a specific language is supported for translation
    
    Returns a dictionary mapping language codes (used in the translate tool) to their full names.
    Use these codes as the source_lang and target_lang parameters in the translate tool.
tools.list_notes:
List all saved notes, optionally filtered by tag.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Retrieving all saved notes
    - Looking for notes with a specific tag
    - Checking what notes are available
    
    Notes are persistent resources managed by the MCP server.
tools.get_note:
Retrieve a specific note by its ID.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Accessing a specific note's content
    - Needing to read a note's details
    
    The note ID must be provided and must be valid.
tools.get_note_by_title:
Find notes by their title, with support for partial matching.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - You need to find notes but don't know the exact ID
    - Searching for notes with similar titles
    - Looking for notes when you remember part of the title
    
    This tool returns a list of notes that match the given title (fully or partially).
    Use the exact_match parameter to control whether to search for exact title matches only.
tools.create_note:
Create a new note with title, content, and optional tags.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Creating a new note to store information
    - Saving important information for later reference
    - Organizing information with tags
    
    The title and content are required. Tags are optional but recommended for organization.
tools.update_note:
Update an existing note by ID.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Modifying a note's title or content
    - Adding or changing tags on a note
    
    Only the fields that need to be updated should be provided.
tools.delete_note:
Delete a note by ID.
    
    Use this tool when:
    - Removing a note that is no longer needed
    
    This operation cannot be undone.

tools.analyze_xid_errors: Analyze NVIDIA GPU XID (eXception ID) errors from kernel logs. XID errors are hardware failures logged by the NVIDIA driver indicating issues like memory corruption, bus failures, or thermal problems. Returns structured error data with severity classifications and SRE-actionable recommendations. Note: May require elevated permissions to read kernel logs.
tools.get_gpu_health: Analyze GPU operational health including temperature, throttling, ECC errors, memory usage, and power consumption. Returns overall health score (0-100) with status assessment and recommendations.
tools.get_gpu_inventory: Returns GPU inventory for all devices. In agent mode: returns local GPU hardware details. In gateway mode: returns cluster-wide inventory with summary (total nodes, GPUs, types) and per-node GPU list. Includes model, UUID, memory, temperature, and utilization. When include_k8s_metadata is true (default in gateway mode), also includes Kubernetes node labels, conditions, and GPU resource allocation counts.
tools.get_nvlink_topology: Get NVLink interconnect topology and health status. Returns GPU-to-GPU NVLink connections, link state, and error counters for multi-GPU systems. Useful for diagnosing silent NVLink degradation.

tools.jmeter_init_plan: Creates a fresh, empty JMX test plan file. This is the first step in creating a JMeter load test.
tools.jmeter_add_thread_group: Adds a Thread Group to a JMX file. This defines a pool of virtual users that will execute the test. Must be called after jmeter_init_plan.
tools.jmeter_add_sampler: Adds an HTTP Sampler (request) to the last Thread Group in a JMX file. This represents an HTTP request that virtual users will execute.
tools.jmeter_add_header: Adds an HTTP Header Manager to the last Thread Group. Headers will be applied to all HTTP samplers within that group.
tools.jmeter_run_test: Executes a JMeter test plan in non-GUI mode. Returns the test results summary. Requires JMeter to be installed and available in PATH.
tools.jmeter_add_listener: Adds a listener to the test plan to collect and display results. Common listeners include Summary Report and View Results Tree.
tools.jmeter_add_timer: Adds a timer to the last Thread Group to introduce delays between requests.
tools.jmeter_add_assertion: Adds a Response Assertion to verify the HTTP response meets expected criteria.

tools.searchRepos: Full-text search across repository names and descriptions
tools.myRepos: List repositories owned by the current user (from .nostr-keys.json)

tools.publishRepoState: Publish repository state to Nostr (kind 30618) - REQUIRES signing

tools.listPRs: List pull requests for a repository
tools.createPR: Create a pull request - REQUIRES signing
tools.createPRViaGittrCLI: Create PR via gittr CLI - full flow including git push (RECOMMENDED for PRs)
tools.getPublicKey: Get public key from private key
tools.submitBounty: Submit work on a bounty (claim it with PR/evidence)

tools.unstarRepo: Unstar a repo (NIP-25 kind 7 on the 30617 event with content "-"). Same tags as starRepo.

tools.unwatchRepo: Unwatch a repo (republish kind 10018 without this repo)
tools.listWatchedRepos: List repos from your latest kind 10018 followed-repos event on relays
tools.getCommitHistory: Get commit history for a repository

tools.listReleases: List git tags from the bridge (refs/tags/*), not Zapstore software releases

tools.publishStatusForRoot: Publish NIP-34 status (1630 open, 1631 merged/applied, 1632 closed, 1633 draft) for an issue, PR, or patch root event
tools.createBountyInvoice: Create Lightning invoice for bounty escrow (POST /api/bounty/create). Use GITTR_LNBITS_* env or pass lnbitsUrl + lnbitsAdminKey. Publish kind 9806 after pay via publishBountyToNostr.
tools.listBountiesForIssue: List kind 9806 bounty events linked to an issue id
tools.getIssueById: Fetch single issue event (1621) by id from relays
tools.getPullRequestById: Fetch single PR event (1618) by id from relays
tools.closeIssue: Convenience: publish status 1632 (closed) for an issue
tools.reopenIssue: Convenience: publish status 1630 (open) for an issue
tools.markPullRequestMerged: Convenience: publish status 1631 (merged/applied) for a PR root event

Tcl REPLs (fc_shell, dc_shell, pt_shell, icc2_shell, tclsh) do NOT need rawMode: tracked mode auto-probes for Tcl, injects the tracking namespace, and pairs with wait-command-completion for immediate completion. Use rawMode=true only for true interactive edge cases (vim, less, btop); it disables status tracking and forces manual capture-pane polling. IMPORTANT: When rawMode=false (default), avoid heredoc syntax (cat << EOF) and other multi-line constructs as they conflict with command wrapping. For file writing, prefer: printf 'content\n' > file, echo statements, or write to temp files instead. For tracked Tcl REPLs the command is wrapped in braces ({command}); multi-word/multi-arg commands work fine, but the command must contain balanced braces (almost all Tcl does). For the rare command with unbalanced braces, use rawMode and verify with capture-pane.
